name: Aaron Guckian
current_role: Former executive director of the Rhode Island Dental Association
bio: Aaron Guckian is the Republican nominee for Governor of Rhode Island; the state Board of Elections certified his 259-vote primary win over Elaine Pelino after turning down her recount request. He was the party's 2022 nominee for lieutenant governor, worked for Governor Donald Carcieri, at the Rhode Island Foundation and at the Rhode Island Dental Association, and chaired the Warwick Sewer Authority. A lifelong East Greenwich resident, he holds degrees from Connecticut College, Rhode Island College and Johnson & Wales University.

platform.point: Pledges to expand housing options, reduce construction barriers, lower utility bills and rein in healthcare costs.
Proposes targeted tax relief, fewer hidden fees and cuts to wasteful state spending.
Would prioritize investment in public schools, teacher support and vocational and technical career pathways.
Plans to address shortages of doctors and dentists through training pipelines, retention incentives and less red tape.
Promises more transparency and a leaner, more business-friendly state government.
Opposes bringing back tolls on trucks.

economy.evidence: Opposes a millionaire's tax and wants to cut state taxes and fees.

liberty.evidence: Personally opposes abortion but treats Rhode Island's abortion law as settled; supports gun rights and opposes the state's assault weapons ban.

immigration.evidence: Supports federal border security while keeping his campaign on state issues; a general statement.

energy.evidence: Focuses on lowering electricity bills, which he calls far too high; a general statement.

education.evidence: General campaign statement prioritizing investment in public schools, teacher support and vocational pathways.

notes: Taxes, energy, abortion, guns and immigration come from an Aug 31, 2026 NBC 10 interview; WPRI and Rhode Island Current block automated reading.

name: Eunice Lehmacher
current_role: Licensed professional counselor and social worker
bio: Eunice Lehmacher is a licensed professional counselor with about 40 years of experience, including private practice, medical and hospice social work, and counseling at Clemson University; she has also worked as a teacher, youth pastor and librarian. She has served on a regional mental health board and Clemson's sustainability advisory committee, and formerly led a local Sierra Club group. Born in Lexington, Missouri, she won the Democratic nomination for SC-3 in June 2026.

platform.point: Aims to lower high prices for working families, small businesses and seniors, and opposes tariffs as a household cost.
Wants more doctors and hospitals, especially in rural areas, and lower health care costs.
Supports affordable childcare, lower college costs and student loan forgiveness.
Seeks to restore housing opportunity and affordability.
Calls for investment in cheaper, cleaner energy, more forests and preservation of natural spaces.
Says billionaires should pay their fair share.
Raises surveillance and privacy concerns about data center expansion.
Favors peace over war and calls for ending what she describes as an unjust war.

economy.evidence: General statement that billionaires should pay their fair share, alongside opposition to tariffs.

welfare.evidence: Supports student loan forgiveness, affordable childcare and more rural doctors and hospitals, without calling for universal programs.

immigration.evidence: General statement criticizing the harshness of ICE enforcement and calling for a more inclusive approach.

foreign.evidence: General statement favoring peace over war and ending a current war she calls unwise.

energy.evidence: Calls for investing in cheaper, cleaner energy and preserving natural spaces; general statement backed by past Sierra Club leadership.

tech.evidence: General statement raising privacy and surveillance concerns about data center growth.

education.evidence: General statement pledging to fight for education and lower college costs, with no stance on school choice.

notes: Searched her ideas, about and news pages and campaign newsletters; the earlier abortion score relied on Ballotpedia, which could not be checked, so liberty was reset to null. No specific stance found on guns, policing or religion in public life.

name: Courtney McClain
bio: Courtney McClain is a Spartanburg native with a journalism degree from the University of South Carolina and a political science master's from Howard University. She led the South Carolina NAACP Youth and College Division and held fellowships with the Congressional Black Caucus Institute and the Clyburn Fellow Program. At 25, she won the Democratic nomination for SC-4.

platform.point: Supports Medicare for All to replace private insurance, and fuller ACA funding in the meantime.
Prioritizes building more affordable housing and guaranteed low-income housing with support services.
Would end the tipped minimum wage and raise the federal minimum wage with annual cost-of-living increases.
Calls for a moratorium on new AI data centers and requiring existing ones to pay their full grid and environmental costs.
Proposes a national teacher pay incentive, more Title I funding and universal free school meals for children in need.
Backs universal background checks, ghost gun rules and a national police misconduct database.
Wants to end detention and deportation as a default and guarantee legal representation for children and asylum seekers.
Supports recognizing a Palestinian state, an arms embargo on Israel and humanitarian aid to Gaza.

economy.evidence: Proposes a higher federal minimum wage indexed to living costs, ending the tipped wage, industry wage floors and stronger IRS enforcement on the rich.

welfare.evidence: Supports Medicare for All replacing private insurance and universal free school meals for children in need.

liberty.evidence: Opposes abortion restrictions and would cosponsor the Equality Act (LGBTQ rights), while backing universal background checks and ghost gun regulation (guns).

security.evidence: Proposes a national police misconduct database, officer transparency rules, diversion programs and an end to private prisons.

immigration.evidence: Wants to end detention and deportation as a default, fund legal representation for asylum seekers and repeal travel restrictions on 38 countries.

foreign.evidence: Supports an arms embargo on Israel and recognition of Palestinian statehood, while backing humanitarian aid to Gaza.

energy.evidence: Wants data centers to pay for their environmental impact and power companies to reinvest profits in the grid, plus flood resilience funding.

tech.evidence: Calls for a moratorium on building new AI data centers and full cost-recovery rules for existing ones.

education.evidence: Proposes a national teacher pay incentive, increased Title I funding, restored special education funding and larger Pell grants.

notes: Scores come from her detailed issue pages on housing, health, wages, growth, schools, public safety and immigration. No stance found on religion in public life.

name: John Peterson
current_role: Banquet supervisor at the North Charleston Convention Center
bio: John Peterson holds a mathematics degree from the State University of New York at Brockport and has worked in customer service management, including for Wegmans in New York; he now works as a banquet supervisor at the North Charleston Convention Center. He is a Charleston County Republican precinct president and has volunteered for Donald Trump's campaigns in several states. He is the Republican nominee challenging Jim Clyburn in SC-6.

platform.point: Would vote for fiscally conservative bills that cut spending, reduce inflation and lower the national debt.
Supports DOGE and pledges to root out fraud, waste and abuse of taxpayer money.
Would champion tough-on-crime bills to keep violent offenders off the streets.
Supports requiring voter ID.
Backs the Trump agenda and opposes any Democratic effort to impeach the president.
Aims to lower gas, grocery and insurance prices.
Opposes a proposed $5,000 dividend to Americans, citing its cost.

economy.evidence: Calls for cutting federal spending, backs government-efficiency cuts and opposes a proposed $5,000 dividend payment.

security.evidence: General pledge to champion tough-on-crime bills that keep violent criminals off the street.

notes: Checked his home, issues and about pages and Live 5 coverage; his issues page lists five brief priorities. No stance found on abortion, guns, immigration, energy, education, foreign policy or health care.

name: John Vincent
current_role: Navy veteran and leadership development consultant
bio: John Vincent is the Democratic nominee for South Carolina's 7th Congressional District. He served 20 years in the U.S. Navy, retiring as a command master chief, and later worked as a leadership development consultant and ran a consulting business. He has been endorsed by the Forward Party and says he will not accept corporate PAC donations.

platform.point: End tariffs, protect Social Security, raise wages and make home ownership more attainable.
Restore small-business programs, give farmers stable trade policy and expand career-focused training.
Keep rural hospitals open and preserve health care tax credits.
Keep commitments made to veterans, teachers and first responders.
Support term limits, a ban on congressional stock trading, limits on dark money and a balanced budget.
Testified against South Carolina Bill 323, calling it harmful to women's reproductive care.
Opposes U.S. military action in Venezuela taken without congressional authorization.
Wants independent economic review, water and power disclosure and enforceable community benefit deals for data centers.

economy.evidence: Wants to end tariffs while also calling for higher wages and budget discipline.

welfare.evidence: Pledges to protect Social Security and health care tax credits and keep rural hospitals open.

liberty.evidence: Abortion: testified against South Carolina Bill 323, saying it would restrict women's reproductive care; no stance found on other liberty issues.

foreign.evidence: Opposes unilateral U.S. military action in Venezuela without Congress or UN approval, while stressing international law and allied opinion.

energy.evidence: Calls for renewable energy requirements, cooling efficiency standards and aquifer and grid disclosure for new data centers.

tech.evidence: Supports data center growth but wants a pause for independent analysis, bans on secrecy agreements and binding community benefit agreements.

notes: Checked his policy, issues and news pages, WMBF and WPDE coverage and the Forward Party endorsement. No stance found on immigration, guns, policing, school choice or religion.

name: Darline Graham
bio: Darline Graham was appointed to the U.S. Senate by Governor Henry McMaster in July 2026 to fill the seat left vacant by the death of her brother, Senator Lindsey Graham, and is the first woman to represent South Carolina in the Senate. She previously worked at the South Carolina Vocational Rehabilitation Department and served as Commissioner of the South Carolina Commission for the Blind from 2019. A native of Central, South Carolina, she holds degrees from the College of Charleston and South Carolina State University.

platform.point: Cosponsors bills expanding U.S.-Israel defense cooperation and countering campus antisemitism.
Backs the Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026.
Cosponsors bills on mandatory E-Verify, ending sanctuary cities and limiting birthright citizenship.
Cosponsors bills restricting abortion medication and permanently barring federal abortion funding.
Backs national concealed-carry reciprocity and removing suppressors from National Firearms Act rules.
Pledges to defend women's and girls' sports under Title IX.
Backs the Protecting American Taxpayers Act to recover unspent COVID funds and extend fraud prosecution deadlines.
Cosponsors the Major Richard Star Act so combat-disabled retirees can receive both retirement pay and VA compensation.

liberty.evidence: Cosponsors abortion restrictions and backs limits on transgender athletes, while supporting looser gun regulation.

security.evidence: Backs the Protecting American Taxpayers Act, which extends the statute of limitations for fraud prosecutions and creates a deepfake scam task force.

immigration.evidence: Cosponsors bills limiting birthright citizenship, mandating E-Verify, defunding sanctuary cities and expanding 287(g).

foreign.evidence: Cosponsors bills deepening U.S.-Israel defense cooperation and introduced Russia sanctions legislation.

photo.file: File:Official portrait of Darline Graham, member of the United States Senate from South Carolina (2026).jpg
photo.author: Rosa Pineda, United States Senate

notes: Reviewed all ten Senate press releases and the campaign site, which stresses her service record and taxpayer stewardship without specific proposals. No stance found on taxes, social programs, energy, tech, schools or religion in public life.

name: Charlie Hatcher
bio: Charlie Hatcher is a fifth-generation dairy farmer and livestock veterinarian who served as Tennessee's Commissioner of Agriculture from 2019 to 2025 under Governor Bill Lee. He holds an animal science degree from Middle Tennessee State University and a veterinary degree from the University of Tennessee, and says he has started eight businesses, including Hatcher Family Dairy. He won the 2026 Republican primary for the 5th District, defeating incumbent Andy Ogles.

platform.point: Describes himself as a pro-gun candidate who will defend Second Amendment rights.
Campaigns as a pro-life candidate.
Pledges to back President Trump, whom he calls the most consequential president of his lifetime.
Wants to dismantle the U.S. Department of Education and return school decisions to states and localities.
Aims to balance the federal budget and reduce the debt by cutting spending and regulations.
Wants to slow farmland loss, improve farm profitability and streamline the H-2A farmworker visa program.
Says he will bring a farmer's work ethic and common sense to Washington.

economy.evidence: Says he wants to balance the budget and reduce federal debt by cutting government spending and regulations.

liberty.evidence: Campaign identifies him as pro-life (abortion) and pro-gun (guns), leaning toward community norms on abortion and individual choice on guns.

immigration.evidence: Calls for legal and reliable avenues for farm labor through a more efficient, less costly H-2A visa program; no stated view on deportation or the border.

education.evidence: Supports dismantling the U.S. Department of Education and returning education decisions to state and local governments.

notes: Checked his campaign site, Wikipedia and its cited Williamson Herald and NBC News coverage; Tennessee Lookout returned 403. No stance found on social programs, policing, foreign policy, energy, tech or religion.

name: Chaz Molder
bio: Chaz Molder has been mayor of Columbia, Tennessee, since 2018, when he unseated the incumbent at 29, and was re-elected in 2022. A graduate of the University of Tennessee and the University of Memphis law school, he highlights eight balanced city budgets without property tax increases and investments in education, public safety and infrastructure. He is the Democratic nominee for Tennessee's 5th District.

platform.point: Supports banning members of Congress from trading individual stocks.
Pledges to make healthcare, housing and groceries more affordable for Tennessee families.
Backs workers' right to organize and stronger labor protections.
Wants to lower healthcare costs, expand coverage, invest in preventive care and keep rural hospitals open.
Cites eight balanced city budgets with no property tax increase and $10.5 million in taxpayer savings.

economy.evidence: Supports workers' organizing rights, stronger labor protections and action on the cost of housing, groceries and healthcare.

welfare.evidence: Calls for broadening health insurance coverage, lowering costs and supporting rural hospitals.

education.evidence: General statement highlighting investment in education as mayor, with no stated view on school choice.

notes: Checked his issues, about and news pages and linked coverage (NewsChannel 5 and ABC links returned 404, Nashville Scene 429, Columbia Daily Herald unreachable). No stance found on abortion, guns, immigration, foreign policy, energy, tech or religion.
